title: Aztec Museum & Pioneer Village to host Farmington UFO Armada presentation
excerpt: Sighting witnessed by many residents, reported in newspapers
content:
More than 75 years after hundreds of mysterious silver objects reportedly filled the skies above Farmington, a local historian and archivist will revisit one of the region’s most enduring mysteries during a presentation at the Aztec Museum & Pioneer Village.

Michael Mongeau, archivist and reference librarian at San Juan College, will present “The 1950 Farmington Armada UFO Incident: Fact or Fiction?” at 6 p.m. Friday.

Drawing on newspaper archives and historical research, Mongeau plans to examine eyewitness accounts of the widely reported sighting, explore possible explanations and discuss evidence suggesting the Farmington area may have been used for early post-World War II drone testing.

“Between March 15-18 of 1950, thousands of local residents witnessed hundreds of silver, disc-shaped objects moving through the skies in broad daylight,” a news release stated. “This event has come to be known as the Farmington Armada.”

Mongeau spoke with Tri-City Record Wednesday and said that he approaches the subject of UFOs with an open mind but leans toward the skeptic side.

“I like to think I fall a little bit kind of more in the middle ground of things,” he said.

Born in Ohio, Mongeau spent most of his youth in Phoenix before developing a passion for history while attending Arizona State University. He went on to earn a degree in history, with a minor in American Indian Studies at Simmons University in Boston and a masters from Barrett, the Honors College at ASU. He worked for various museums and libraries in Arizona, including the Heard Museum Library, Phoenix Trolley Museum and Pueblo Grande Museum.

Eventually, Mongeau took his passion for libraries to Boston, where he studied at Simmons University, earning two masters degrees in library and information science (with a focus on archives) and history. In Boston, he worked for institutions including the Boston Architectural College, city of Somerville and Rogerson Communities.

“I wanted to come back to the Southwest to be closer to family (in Phoenix),” he said.

Mongeau said his interest in UFO’s began with an investigation of the Aztec UFO Crash incident and led to presentations at San Juan College and at the Aztec Museum.

“They were both incredibly successful events,” Mongeau said. “And so I figured, well, you know, if people really enjoyed hearing about Aztec, why not talk about the other major UFO event that occurred, kind of in the general area.”

The UFO incident in Farmington was covered by the Daily Times. Mongeau said that newspaperarchive.com has an archive of the Daily Times and the San Juan Independent that dates back to the late 1800s.

Mongeau, who is now booked for a number of presentations on the topic, said when he lived in Boston and Phoenix he never thought he’d be investigating UFOs and aliens. His focus was always on Native Americans.
